definition: Doctor shopping is a behavior in which a person gets overlapping prescriptions for the same drug from more than one prescriber so they can obtain larger amounts than any one prescriber intended. It is used as a marker of prescription drug abuse and can also contribute to diversion to the black market.

reasons: The definition is supported on the core sense of "doctor shopping" as overlapping prescriptions from multiple prescribers to obtain higher doses than intended by individual prescribers, and on its role in supplying the black market, but the field "learning" is not supported by the packet's content, which is about prescription drug abuse monitoring and addictovigilance rather than learning.

The packet says doctor shopping “involves overlapping prescriptions from multiple prescribers for the same drug, to obtain higher doses than those prescribed by each prescriber on an individual basis,” but it does not support the specific phrasing “larger amounts than any one prescriber intended.”

The packet supports that doctor shopping “may play an important role in supplying the black market,” but it does not explicitly support the definition’s wording “contribute to diversion to the black market.”
